newsitem.title: UK: SFO to resist any move to quash Saunders verdict.
newsitem.headline: SFO to resist any move to quash Saunders verdict.

text.p: The UK's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) said on Tuesday it would resist any attempt to overturn the conviction of former Guinness chairman Ernest Saunders.

Earlier the European Court of Human Rights ruled that Britain had denied a fair trial to Saunders, who was convicted of fraud in 1990, because evidence obtained from him by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) inspectors was later used against him in a criminal prosecution.

"(The court) said it could not speculate on whether the outcome of the trial would have been any different had use not been made of the (DTI) transcripts by the prosecution, and its finding of a breach of Article 6 was not to be taken to suggest this. We shall therefore, resist any attempt to overturn Ernest Saunders' conviction," the SFO said in a statement.
The SFO said the case had been "heard exhaustively in the English courts" and two appeal court hearings had upheld the prosecution's case.

Saunders, now 61, was convicted on 12 counts including false accounting and theft for inflating Guinness' share price to help its 1986 takeover of whisky group Distillers Plc prevail against rival bidder Argyll Plc.
